name: Fuzzing & Automated Testing
description: Fuzzing techniques, coverage-guided testing, and bug-finding pipelines.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this list focused on making fuzzing smarter and broadening where it could be applied. A central problem in 2018 was that pure fuzzing struggles to get past complex input checks, which "QSYM: A Practical Concolic Execution Engine Tailored for Hybrid Fuzzing" (2018) addressed by pairing fast fuzzing with a streamlined concolic engine so hard branches could be solved on demand. At the same time, researchers pushed fuzzing into systems software: "MoonShine: Optimizing OS Fuzzer Seed Selection with Trace Distillation" (2018) attacked the OS system-call interface by distilling good seeds, marking an early move toward kernel and driver targets.

The 2019-2021 period was about sharpening the feedback signal and reaching new domains. "GREYONE: Data Flow Sensitive Fuzzing" (2020) showed that tracking how input bytes flow to comparisons lets a fuzzer mutate the right bytes, while "EcoFuzz: Adaptive Energy-Saving Greybox Fuzzing as a Variant of the Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandit" (2020) and "SyzVegas: Beating Kernel Fuzzing Odds with Reinforcement Learning" (2021) recast scheduling decisions as learning problems. The community also expanded targets dramatically: "FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation" (2019) tackled embedded firmware, "USBFuzz: A Framework for Fuzzing USB Drivers by Device Emulation" (2020) hit driver interfaces, and "Nyx: Greybox Hypervisor Fuzzing using Fast Snapshots and Affine Types" (2021) brought fast snapshotting to hypervisors. A parallel thread automated the human work of fuzzing itself, with "FuzzGen: Automatic Fuzzer Generation" (2020) and "APICraft: Fuzz Driver Generation for Closed-source SDK Libraries" (2021) generating the harnesses libraries need.

By 2022-2023 the frontier moved toward stateful and structured targets that simple coverage feedback handles poorly. "Stateful Greybox Fuzzing" (2022) and "StateFuzz: System Call-Based State-Aware Linux Driver Fuzzing" (2022) made fuzzers reason about program and protocol state, and "Bleem: Packet Sequence Oriented Fuzzing for Protocol Implementations" (2023) extended this to whole packet sequences. Hardware and compilers also became first-class targets, with "TheHuzz: Instruction Fuzzing of Processors Using Golden-Reference Models for Finding Software-Exploitable Vulnerabilities" (2022) and "FuzzJIT: Oracle-Enhanced Fuzzing for JavaScript Engine JIT Compiler" (2023) using reference models and oracles to catch bugs coverage alone would miss.

Most recently, large language models have entered the pipeline from both sides. "LLM-Fuzzer: Scaling Assessment of Large Language Model Jailbreaks" (2024) turns fuzzing on LLMs themselves to find jailbreaks, while "Fuzzing BusyBox: Leveraging LLM and Crash Reuse for Embedded Bug Unearthing" (2024) uses an LLM to drive classic embedded bug-finding. Together these mark a shift from hand-tuned mutation strategies toward learned and model-assisted fuzzing across an ever-wider range of targets.

milestones.title: FuzzGen: Automatic Fuzzer Generation
milestones.note: automated the labor-intensive step of writing fuzz harnesses for libraries
